newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kolbenschmidt says T&N link is "wishful thinking".
newsitem.headline: Kolbenschmidt says T&N link is "wishful thinking".

text.p: German car components manufacturer Kolbenschmidt AG on Friday described suggestions that Britain's T&N Plc might still be able to craft a link-up with it as "wishful thinking".

Earlier this week German engineering and defence group Rheinmetall AG appeared to deal a blow to T&N's long-running ambition to take over Kolbenschmidt by taking a strategic 24.99 percent stake in the firm.

Industry sources have however suggested that Rheinmetall's move might yet prove friendly to T&N's own quest to combine its pistons business with that of Kolbenschmidt, with some mooting a three-way joint venture as possible.
"Any talk that Rheinmetall might cooperate with T&N is wishful thinking. If you speak to Rheinmetall it will deny it too," a Kolbenschmidt spokesman said in response to enquiries.
Rheinmetall, which announced on Wednesday its plans to seek management control in Kolbenschmidt, was not immediately available to comment.
T&N retains options on a separate 24.99 percent stake in Kolbenschmidt but has been so far been prevented from taking up the stake by the German Federal Cartel Office.
It has argued that such a move would would lead to a full takeover bid by T&N which, if successful, would give it an overly dominant position in key areas of the car components sector.
T&N had been hoping for a cartels committee of the German Court of Appeal to give it the go-ahead to take up its options in Kolbenschmidt, thus reversing the earlier decision by the cartel office.

But an appeals court spokeswoman said the court had earlier this week merely decided to continue its study into the matter and was issuing a court order to take new evidence on whether the purchase of a majority of Kolbenschmidt by T&N would constitute a potential monopoly situation.
Involved parties, which will include German customers of both T&N and Kolbenschmidt, have been asked to present information on their relationship with the suppliers by April 15.
